consistency_checks.detail: BP meets definition of resistant hypertension and three antihypertensives are documented.
RBC, Hct, and Hb values demonstrate a falling normocytic anemia.
Prior NSTEMI and ongoing dual antiplatelet therapy are clearly recorded.
eGFR, serum creatinine, and urine ACR are missing, limiting assessment of CKD.

top_concerns: CAD is mis‑framed as a differential rather than a known comorbidity.
Probabilities for OSA and anemia of chronic disease were underestimated.
Secondary hypertension causes were grouped together, obscuring individual work‑up priorities.
Key laboratory tests (eGFR, urine ACR, iron studies, aldosterone/renin) are missing.
recommended_primary: Obstructive sleep apnea (as the leading secondary cause of resistant hypertension)
review_summary: The differential captures the major clinical themes but misclassifies known CAD, under‑weights OSA and anemia of chronic disease, and lumps distinct secondary‑hypertension etiologies. Adjusted probabilities and explicit separation of secondary causes improve diagnostic focus and align the work‑up with the critical laboratory abnormalities.
